principle: The report should feel like a high-level tennis lesson: instant diagnosis first, visible proof second, one cue and one practice task next, technical evidence on demand.
headline_patterns: Your {not_problem} is fine. The leak starts at {actual_problem}.
This isn't a {surface_symptom} problem. It starts with {root_cause}.
Your best reps already show the answer: {self_best_difference}.
This works on {good_context}; {fail_context} is where it breaks down.
language_guardrails: Never say 'always' or 'never' for technique unless it is truly a rule/safety condition.
Distinguish observation from interpretation without sounding robotic: direct for high-confidence evidence; 'it looks like'/'likely' when needed.
Use tennis consequence language: space, time, contact options, margin, depth, direction, spin, pace and recovery.
Avoid the words metric, causal graph, recurrence, pose model and interpretation confidence in player mode.
No fake praise. Every 'good', 'strong', 'clean' or 'excellent' statement must point to an evidenced strength.
One card = one coaching priority. Secondary issues stay collapsed until the primary correction is understood.
A visual caption should sound like something a coach might say while pausing the video and should normally fit in eight words.
Do not quote or imitate named coaches; synthesize general elite-coaching communication patterns.

coach_like_behavior: ask for a constrained set of reps
